summary: Peak-hour dynamic tariff applied to reserved-capacity hybrid job; customer billed premium rate
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightGuide Inc. reports a premium 'peak-hour dynamic tariff' line on their finalized invoice for a mixed-hosted/dedicated inference job that ran across the 18:00–19:00 US‑EST peak window. They claim the workload was pinned to their reserved Dedicated pool and should have been billed at the reserved rate without peak surcharge.

Impact: One high-volume nightly batch job (~1.2M tokens) billed with a 1.5x peak tariff for ~22 minutes (partial window), resulting in an unexpected charge of $4,300. Customer requests correction or credit and a root-cause explanation. This is affecting their finance team and could impact renewal conversations.

Environment: prod/us-east-1, Dedicated pool: brightguide-dedicated-01, Job ID: bg-20260309-embed-11, Invoice: INV-2026-03-09-BG.

Steps to reproduce / immediate checks performed by support: 1) Reviewed job metadata and saw reserved_pool_id present in job manifest. 2) Checked routing logs — job shows a short sequence of requests routed to hosted fallback (hosted-us-east) between 2026-03-09T22:38:12Z and 2026-03-09T22:60:45Z. 3) Queried meter tags for affected requests; several entries had pricing_tag=null. 4) Compared Console estimate (shows reserved rate) vs finalized invoice (shows peak-tariff line).

Attached logs/links: routing trace (link), meter dump snapshot (link), invoice line item screenshot (link).

Hypothesis: A transient edge/proxy rotation dropped the pricing_tag on a subset of requests during a reserved->hosted fallback window. The tariff-windowing engine matched those requests to the 'peak-hour' pricing because region tag and pricing_tag were missing, which triggered dynamic surcharge and reclassified warmup requests as billable at peak-hosted rates. This also appears to have double-counted a small number of KV-cache warmup tokens due to a dedupe TTL expiry.

Requested outcome: Customer requests a credit for the peak surcharge (~$4,300) and correction of any duplicated warmup tokens. They also want confirmation of mitigation steps to prevent recurrence.

Pricing middleware returned 503 on initial attach, causing fallback to hosted route. Logged potential issue: pricing_tag propagation is not retried on transient proxy restarts.

2026-03-11 16:09 - SRE (Marco): Deployed hotfix to staging and observed no null pricing_tag on simulated proxy restarts. Plan: deploy to prod in maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Will monitor for any further routed-to-hosted anomalies.

resolution: Investigating; provisional credit approved pending prod patch verification
next_steps: 1) Deploy hotfix to prod on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. 2) Monitor routing traces for 4 hours post-deploy for any hosted fallback spikes. 3) If no further anomalies, issue credit memo and update customer. 4) Backfill a postmortem and add runbook step to detect null pricing_tag regressions.
investigation_notes: Edge-proxy rotation at 22:38:11Z caused pricing metadata lookup to return transient error for ~22 seconds. Requests that hit that window had pricing_tag=null and were routed through tariff-window service which defaulted to dynamic peak tariff. A dedupe TTL for KV-cache warmup fingerprints (previously 30s) expired at boundary and allowed a small set of warmup requests to be billed twice. Change set increases TTL to 90s and adds a pricing_tag reattach retry. Linked INT-3305 for infra follow-up.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12: Sent email to finance@brightguide.com confirming provisional credit and schedule for fix. Provided log snippets showing the routed-to-hosted window and promised full postmortem within 5 business days after prod verification.
